title: docmeta stewardship vocabulary (1.0.0-proposal.1)
description: Is this page cared for: ownership, review, and the anchors that make drift detectable. Every field is a fact only a human can assert — dates the repo can derive (creation, last change) are deliberately absent, because git owns them and hand-typed copies go stale. The review dates are records, not freshness gates: JSON Schema cannot compare a date to today, and deriving the due date from `last-reviewed` + `review-interval` belongs to tooling that can read a clock (any freshness grader reads `last-reviewed`).

owner.description: The person or team answerable for this page — the one required field of every docs-ownership system from Backstage to GitLab. A name, a handle, a chat channel, a team slug, or a list of them; write the spelling people can actually reach.

stakeholders.description: Who has a stake in this page being right: the feature's engineer, the product owner, the support lead who fields its tickets. The standing parties to consult before changing the page — where `reviewed-by` records who actually did the last pass. Page-level on purpose: the right stakeholders differ page by page, and project-wide ones belong in your project docs, not in every file's frontmatter.

reviewed-by.description: Who last reviewed the page. Named `reviewed-by` rather than `reviewers` because MyST already defines `reviewers` as scholarly person objects.

last-reviewed.description: When the page was last reviewed, as a W3CDTF date. The field freshness tooling reads to derive review deadlines. A record, not a freshness gate — JSON Schema cannot compare a date to today.

review-interval.description: How often the page should be reviewed, as an ISO 8601 duration: `P90D`, `P1Y`. ISO rather than `90d` so the value is machine-comparable. With `last-reviewed`, this is everything review tooling needs to derive the due date — a stored due date would only ever agree with them or lie.

verified-against.description: The product version, API revision, or spec the content was last verified against — `operator 1.4.2`. What turns 'reviewed' into 'reviewed against something'.

source-of-truth.description: Where reality lives for this page: a repo path, an API spec, a schema file. The anchor a drift check compares the page against; a page without one cannot be drift-monitored.

stringList.description: One non-empty string, or a non-empty list of unique ones — the same shape as kg's labelList.

w3cdtf.description: A W3CDTF date, permitting reduced precision: `2026`, `2026-08`, `2026-08-23`, or a full timestamp — in which case the timezone designator is required, as the W3CDTF profile itself mandates (no local-time form). Field-ranged (month 01-12, day 01-31, hour 00-23) so an impossible date fails here rather than becoming Invalid Date in the tooling that derives review deadlines; not calendar-exact — February 31 is a reviewer's catch.
